models.label: ECMWF IFS 0.25°
models.note: ECMWF's operational physics model, open-data release. Its gust field is a maximum over the output interval, not an instantaneous value, so gust factors look large in light air.

models.label: ECMWF AIFS
models.note: ECMWF's machine-learning model - a genuinely independent opinion. Publishes no gust field, so gusts come from IFS and ICON-2i only.

models.label: ItaliaMeteo ICON-2i
models.note: ItaliaMeteo / ARPAE high-resolution model for Italy - the finest grid available here. Runs only ~60-72 h ahead and updates every 12 h, so it drops out of the longer-range view.

models.label: Météo-France MFWAM
models.note: Full sea-state decomposition - total wave, wind wave and swell with heights, directions and periods.

models.label: ECMWF WAM 0.25°
models.note: Total significant wave height only - used to cross-check MFWAM.

briefing.headline: Benign, near-windless pattern over the Aeolians - 2-7 kt and under a foot of sea, but it is far too early to bank on it.
briefing.synopsis: No organised pressure gradient over the islands. The consensus across all available models, sampled every 6 h, has wind at 1-7 kt at every island through 3 Oct, backing and veering through the whole compass - southerly 170-200 degrees overnight at Portorosa, swinging N to NNE by midday - which is the signature of a slack field with land/sea breeze doing most of the work. Waves and swell sit at 0.1-0.8 ft everywhere, with Stromboli's 0.8 ft at 06:00 on 1 Oct the largest figure in the dataset. ECMWF IFS and AIFS (both 01 Oct 06Z) and ICON-2i (01 Oct 12Z) agree on the light regime; the only flagged spread is Panarea at 06:00 on 1 Oct, where models range 3.3-9.8 kt.
briefing.overnight_anchorage: The fleet is not aboard yet. For the 3 Oct night at Portorosa the only listed option, Portorosa Marina, scores 1.0 - enclosed, all-round shelter - on 4 kt SE, gusting 8.6 kt, with 0.1 ft swell from the NNW. Nothing in the payload would push the fleet elsewhere, and with that berth the choice does not matter anyway.
briefing.tomorrow_morning: For the first leg, Portorosa to Lipari on 4 Oct, the payload recommends a 06:00 departure: 4.8 kt SSE, gusts 11.3 kt, 0.1 ft sea, dead downwind at 178 TWA - motoring weather for a 22 nm hop. Wind swings to NNE by midday and goes close-hauled at 3-5 kt, so there is no meaningful wind-driven reason to prefer one window over another, only daylight and arrival time. Treat all of this as pattern, not plan: departure is two days out and these legs sit 72-120 h ahead.

passage_notes.note: Verdict go in every window; 2-5 kt, 0.1 ft sea. Recommended 06:00, SSE run. Expect engine.
Go throughout; 3-5 kt WNW-NW beam/close reach, 0.1 ft. 12 nm, no timing constraint shown.
Go throughout; 3-5 kt NW beam reach, 0.1 ft over 26 nm. Berth there is the weak link, not the passage.
Go; 4-6 kt N-NNE broad reach to run, 0.1-0.3 ft.
Go; 4-6 kt E-ENE dead downwind, 0.3 ft, 28 nm. Edge of the forecast horizon (reaches 7 Oct 23:00).

cautions: Everything beyond about 3 Oct is pattern, not forecast. Stability statistics show mean direction shifts of 65 degrees between runs at 72-120 h lead - the trip-date wind directions above will change, even if the light speeds hold.
Panarea, 1 Oct 06:00: models disagree by more than 6 kt (range 3.3-9.8 kt). Worth noting the models are not locked together even at short range.

Marina del Gabbiano, Stromboli (5 Oct) is rated workable, not sheltered - open from every direction, no anchoring, and its shelter depends entirely on the calm holding. If the pattern firms up at all before that night, reconsider the optional Stromboli leg in favour of Panarea.
IFS gust values are interval maxima, so figures like 15.7 kt against a 5 kt mean look dramatic in light air and are reported, not treated as a caution.
briefing.confidence_note: IFS, AIFS and ICON-2i all agree on a light, gradient-free regime and run-to-run wind-speed shifts are small (0.7 kt mean at 72-120 h), but the 65-degree mean direction shift at that lead time means the specific wind angles for the trip dates are not yet trustworthy.
